summary.text: 作 combines the person side form 亻 with 乍. Its common meanings include ‘make,’ ‘work,’ and ‘act’; 乍 is traditionally analyzed as a sound element, though whether it supplied the sound when 作 was first formed is unresolved.

formation.text: 作 is conventionally analyzed as a phonosemantic graph: 人, written in its side form 亻, is treated as a semantic marker, and 乍 as a sound element. The received Shuowen text says 从人从乍 and glosses 作 as ‘rise, begin’; Duan Yucai’s commentary explicitly calls 乍 phonetic. Another analysis proposes 人 was added to distinguish the work/action graph 作 from uses of 乍 meaning ‘suddenly’ or ‘temporarily.’ That account does not establish whether 乍 supplied the sound at the graph’s formation.

components.text: 亻 is the conventional side form of 人. One analysis treats 人 as a semantic marker distinguishing 作, associated with work or action, from 乍 uses meaning ‘suddenly’ or ‘temporarily’; it does not identify a particular person or maker.

乍 is conventionally treated as the sound element in 作. Analyses of its early graph disagree: one interprets it as clearing vegetation, another as a garment lapel. Neither establishes the depicted object’s name or pronunciation.

sound_limitation.text: The cited Middle Chinese pair is 乍 dzraeH and 作 tsak; the cited Old Chinese forms differ in onset and rhyme, 乍 *[dz]ˤrak-s and 作 *[ts]ˤak, and the Mandarin pair is zhà and zuò. These comparisons do not establish the historical sound change linking the forms.

sound.text: The cited readings are listed as Middle Chinese values; the evidence does not explain their historical relationship.
The cited Old Chinese reconstructions differ in onset and rhyme; the evidence does not give the sound change connecting them.
Modern Mandarin readings provide a comparison but do not establish the ancient phonetic relationship.

history.text: The received Shuowen entry analyzes 作 as 从人从乍 and glosses it 起也, ‘rise, begin.’ Its head text does not explicitly identify 乍 as phonetic; that analysis appears in Duan Yucai’s commentary.

One analysis reports early 乍 uses associated with clearing vegetation and building a settlement, and proposes that 人 was added to distinguish the work/action graph 作 from uses of 乍 meaning ‘suddenly’ or ‘temporarily.’ Another account calls 乍 an earlier graph for 作. These proposals do not establish a single graphic sequence.

The selected seal-script image is a modern vector rendering of 乍 in a seal-script tradition, not a dated artifact or an early form of 作. It illustrates the related graph without establishing how 作 formed.

A proposal identifying a discussed oracle-bone graph as an early form of 作 was rejected as insufficiently supported. The dispute does not settle the identity of every early graph or reading associated with 作.

uncertainties.text: The evidence does not settle the date or sequence of the 人+乍 construction, whether 乍 supplied the sound when 作 formed, or the sound change connecting the cited reconstructions. Competing interpretations of 乍’s early graphic form also leave the depicted object’s name and pronunciation unresolved.

Reported early uses include clearing, settlement building, casting, and making, while Shuowen records ‘rise, begin.’ The sequence linking these uses is unresolved, and the supplied evidence does not identify an earliest attested sense of 作.

senses.text: Early examples associated with 乍/作 writing include clearing land, building a settlement, casting, and broader making or action. These support a work/action range but do not establish the earliest dated use of 作 itself.

senses.period: Shuowen lexicographic record; date of use unresolved
senses.text: The Shuowen glosses 作 as 起, ‘rise’ or ‘begin.’ A separate discussion reads 作 as ‘arise/recover’ in a disputed oracle-bone phrase; that reading does not settle the identity of all early forms.
Current glosses include making, working, composing or writing, and acting or performing. The evidence here does not establish the full chronology from older uses.

developments.text: The current meanings of making, working, and acting are consistent with an extension of the reported work/action range, though intermediate steps are not documented.

limitations.text: The cited early examples are not dated here, and the evidence does not establish an earliest use of 作 or a complete chronology for its current meanings.

overview.text: 作 combines a person marker with 乍 and commonly means ‘make,’ ‘work,’ or ‘act.’ 乍 is traditionally treated as its sound element, though its role in the graph’s original formation remains uncertain.

components.text: 亻 is the person marker; one account says it distinguishes 作’s work/action use from 乍’s sudden or temporary uses.
乍 is conventionally treated as the sound element, though the historical sound link to 作 is unresolved.

relationships.text: In the 人+乍 analysis, 人 is proposed as a semantic marker distinguishing 作’s work/action use from 乍’s sudden or temporary uses; it is not said to identify a particular person or maker. 亻 is the conventional side form in 作.

Dictionary analyses and the Shuowen commentary treat 乍 as the sound element in 作. The cited readings are real comparisons, but their reconstructions differ and the evidence does not establish the sound change linking them; this role is not certain for the graph’s initial formation.
